examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For row-major arrays, rightmost indices vary fastest: A[i][j] has element offset iC+j in an R×C array. Compare access order with page/cache block size. A column loop can revisit more distinct pages than available frames even when consecutive rows share a page.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A zero-based int A[10][20] has four-byte elements and base address 1000. What is the address of A[3][7]?

**Answer: 1268.** Element offset=3·20+7=67. Byte offset=67·4=268. Address=1000+268=1268. The column count 20, not the row count 10, determines row stride.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Partial C aggregate initialization zero-fills unspecified elements. Reading beyond an array boundary remains invalid even if adjacent memory happens to exist.

Array capacity and the number of currently stored elements are separate quantities.
